title: Create Charmbracelet TUI version of Impostor Game
description:
Build a terminal version of Impostor Game using Charmbracelet libraries. It should support both an interactive Bubble Tea TUI and non-interactive flag-based CLI flows for scripting/automation.

Scope:
- Add a TUI command/entrypoint for hosting and playing from the terminal.
- Use Bubble Tea for the interactive event loop and Lip Gloss for styling.
- Use Bubbles components where useful, such as list/table/textinput/viewport/spinner.
- Consider Huh forms for setup flows like player name, room code, category, and rounds.
- Preserve the existing web game behavior and rules.
- Support non-interactive flags for core actions so the game can be scripted or driven from shell commands.

Interactive TUI ideas:
- Home screen: create room, join room, show rules/help.
- Lobby screen: show players, ready states, category, rounds, host actions.
- Role screen: reveal word or IMPOSTOR privately.
- Turn screen: show current speaker and turn order.
- Discussion/voting screen: select suspected impostor.
- Results screen: reveal impostor, secret word, votes, and next-round/finish actions.

Non-interactive CLI ideas:
- Create room with flags.
- Join room with room code/name flags.
- Set category/rounds as host.
- Mark ready.
- Vote.
- Query current room/player state as JSON for automation.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented TUI command exists and can run locally.
- Interactive flow covers creating/joining a room and playing a full round.
- Non-interactive flag mode supports at least create/join/ready/state/vote actions.
- Terminal UI is readable on common terminal sizes and handles resize events.
- Existing web UI and websocket behavior continue to work.
- Tests cover command parsing and key game-state transitions used by the TUI/CLI.

Notes:
- Follow the Charmbracelet skill guidance: Bubble Tea Model/Update/View pattern, Lip Gloss styles, Bubbles components, and Huh forms where appropriate.
- Keep implementation PG/kid-friendly and consistent with the existing party-game tone.
design: Architecture plan: split core game rules from transports. Keep existing web/websocket server as one transport and add terminal clients as another. Introduce an internal game/domain layer for rooms, players, phases, categories, turns, voting, and view snapshots; keep privacy enforced by per-player views. Add a small client protocol layer for websocket messages shared by browser, TUI, and flag CLI. Add cmd/impostor-game command structure with serve, tui, and CLI actions. TUI uses Bubble Tea Model/Update/View and talks to the same websocket API. Non-interactive mode uses the same client/protocol and prints JSON for automation. Host flow can either connect to an existing server or start an embedded local server for local play.
close_reason: Implemented Charmbracelet TUI, embedded/local server option, non-interactive CLI actions, docs, and tests.

title: Update tests for direct voting and draft vote flow
description: Cover the new turn-to-voting transition and draft/final vote behavior with automated tests.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert final turn enters voting; draft votes are accepted during turns; draft votes can be changed; draft votes do not end voting or count as final votes; submitting final votes moves to results when everyone has voted.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add voting confirmation flow using draft votes
description: When voting begins, players with a saved draft vote should see a confirmation screen allowing them to submit that vote or change it before final submission. Players without a draft vote should see a Vote Now screen. Players who have submitted final votes should wait for others.
acceptance_criteria: Voting screen shows confirm-submit UI when a draft vote exists; players can change the selected target before submitting; final vote locks after submit; voted players see a waiting state; results appear only after all final votes are submitted.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add draft vote selection during turns
description: Allow players to select and change a draft impostor guess while turns are still in progress. Draft votes should be visible only as each player's own current guess and must not count toward results until submitted as a final vote.
acceptance_criteria: During turns, each player can pick a suspected impostor; the selection is saved as a draft vote; players can change the draft during turns; draft votes do not populate final vote counts or mark players as voted.
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove discussion phase from game flow
description: Eliminate the separate discussion screen/phase so the game transitions directly from turns to voting after the final turn. Update backend phase transitions, frontend phase routing/previews, and remove the host-only Start Voting action.
acceptance_criteria: After the final doneTurn, room phase is voting; no discussion screen is rendered or selectable in preview; startVoting is no longer needed; docs no longer describe discussion as a separate phase.
close_reason: Closed

title: Carry code query param from home to join screen
description: If a user lands on the home page with a code query param, e.g. /?code=abc, the app should preserve that room code when they tap Join Room and prepopulate the Join Room code input.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /?code=abc shows the home screen; tapping Join Room navigates to the join screen with abc prefilled; /?screen=join&code=abc continues to work; /?screen=join&room=abc continues to work.
close_reason: Implemented with test

title: Randomize starting player each round
description: The player who starts speaking in the turns phase should be random for each round/game instead of always following the same room join order from the first player. This keeps the game fair and less predictable.
acceptance_criteria: When a round starts, the first currentTurnId is randomly selected from the players in the room; the turn order then proceeds through all players exactly once from that randomized starting point or a shuffled order; repeated rounds can start with different players; all clients see the same turn order/current player; existing refresh/resume behavior still restores the correct current turn.
close_reason: Implemented with tests

title: Allow host to remove players from room
description: Hosts should be able to remove/kick a player from the room, especially from the lobby when someone joins by mistake, duplicates their session, or becomes disruptive/offline. The UI should expose a host-only remove action next to non-host players and the backend should remove that player from room state and notify clients.
acceptance_criteria: In the lobby, the host sees a remove/kick control for each non-host player; non-host users do not see remove controls; clicking remove asks for confirmation; confirmed removal deletes the player from the room player list and turn order; removed player's connected client is returned to the home/join flow or shown a clear removed message; host cannot remove themselves via this control; game state remains consistent after removal.
close_reason: Implemented with tests

title: Support code query param on join screen
description: When visiting the app with a join URL, the room code input should be prepopulated from a code query argument. Example: http://54.196.177.53/?screen=join&code=abc should render the Join Room screen with abc already filled in. This should work alongside the existing room query param/session URL handling.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /?screen=join&code=abc shows the Join Room screen; the room code input contains ABC/abc; joining uses that value without retyping; existing /?screen=join&room=abc behavior still works; refresh does not clear the prefilled code.
close_reason: Implemented with tests
